bug_semantics: EtherNet/IP TCP/44818 Encapsulation::ReceiveTcpMsg() in source/src/enet_encap/encap.cc reads a 24-byte encapsulation header into the global receive buffer, then if the header's declared payload length exceeds remaining BufWriter capacity (1776 bytes when CIPSTER_ETHERNET_BUFFER_SIZE is 1800) it drains the oversized body through disposeOfLargePacket() without storing it, but still returns remaining + ENCAPSULATION_HEADER_LENGTH as a successful full-packet length. HandleDataOnTcpSocket() in source/src/enet_encap/networkhandler.cc accepts any num_read >= 24 and constructs BufReader(s_buf, num_read) with no upper bound against sizeof(s_buf). BufReader stores limit = start + aCount with no object-size check, so get16() only bounds against that forged limit. After a prior request primes s_buf[24..] with a crafted CPF layout, an oversized SendRRData on the same session refreshes only the 24-byte header; HandleReceivedExplicitTcpData() then slices command = aCommand + headerz and Cpf::DeserializeCpf() walks item_count/type/length via BufReader::get16() until it reads one byte immediately past s_buf (ASan global-buffer-overflow). Demonstrated impact is unauthenticated remote DoS. CVE.org state is PUBLISHED; NVD vulnStatus is Deferred, not rejected; GHSA withdrawn_at is null; vendor closed liftoff-sr/CIPster#46 as completed via commit e8e9dba ('Fixes #46').
flaw_origin: The oversized-body drain existed since 90721b00e44e461d14501bb20714a4d71d9e18e4 (2018-07-24), but that path returned disposeOfLargePacket()'s 0 on success (or -1 on recv failure). HandleDataOnTcpSocket already treated num_read < ENCAPSULATION_HEADER_LENGTH (24) as error, so discarded packets were not parsed. The smallest first-write of the flawed mechanism is d442e60357a8280c73884d262192f67b82bc2949 (2018-08-08), a regular single-parent commit that replaced `return disposeOfLargePacket(aSocket, remaining)` with `if (disposeOfLargePacket(...) != remaining) return kEipStatusError; else return remaining + ENCAPSULATION_HEADER_LENGTH`. Immediate parent e38047cb334362eb630804b65f070d7a1abb2f4c still returns the drain helper's 0/-1 and lacks that fake-success expression anywhere in its tree. git log -L on the oversized branch shows no later rewrite of those return lines until the 2026 fix. Not a move, squash, revert, or backport.

reasoning: The advisory names a real, vendor-patched out-of-bounds read on the TCP encapsulation receive path, not a withdrawn/rejected CVE. Root cause is not CPF's willingness to parse a large item_count; it is ReceiveTcpMsg reporting a full stored length after it had already discarded the body, so HandleDataOnTcpSocket builds a BufReader whose logical window exceeds s_buf and DeserializeCpf walks off the object. The BIC is the first write of that fake-success return: d442e60357a8280c73884d262192f67b82bc2949. Its parent still returned 0/-1 from disposeOfLargePacket, which the existing num_read < 24 check treated as failure, so the parent is not vulnerable to this mechanism. 90721b00 introduced the drain helper but not the bogus success length, and is therefore not the BIC. d442e60 is a regular single-parent 2018 commit, not a squash/move/revert aggregate; later encap.cc commits until e8e9dba did not rewrite the return. AI judgment is from that BIC commit object only: human author/committer Dick Hollenbeck, no co-author or generator trailers, dated years before coding assistants. Later AI-looking issue text, Copilot-era refactors, and the 2026 fix are irrelevant to BIC attribution. Verdict is NOT_AI.
